prompt: Mayonnaise is oil and water-based liquid beaten together into a stable, creamy mixture that does not separate, thanks to egg yolk. Egg yolk works because it acts as:

options.text: An acid that dissolves the oil into the water
A preservative that stops the oil going off
A thickener that simply makes everything too stiff to separate
An emulsifier whose molecules coat tiny oil droplets and keep them dispersed in the water instead of joining back together

explanation: Egg yolk contains lecithin, an emulsifier with a water-loving end and a fat-loving end. It coats small oil droplets and stops them coalescing, keeping the oil-in-water emulsion of mayonnaise stable.
